RECORDING_LIMITATION: Transcription of a direct chat decision in the Claude Code session; the user's reply is verbatim, the options are the agent's own wording as presented to the user.
CONTEXT: During F01 the user asked whether Windows testing is needed at all for a Firefox add-on. The agent explained the technical position (mostly platform-neutral public APIs; observed platform differences in window geometry, WebApp/Taskbar Tab windows and resource behavior) and that the bound Technical Foundation (T01; r6 §§9.1/9.3, measurement 'je Lastprofil und Betriebssystem') requires both operating systems, so a change is a material Technical Foundation change. Three options were presented.

OPTIONS_PRESENTED.1: Keep as bound: Windows remains fully in V1 scope including performance evidence.
OPTIONS_PRESENTED.2: Windows without performance evidence: Windows remains a supported V1 platform with functional tests; performance/resource measurements (calibration, R500/R2000) only on Ubuntu; the resource promise then applies to Ubuntu only.
OPTIONS_PRESENTED.3: V1 Ubuntu only: Windows not promised or tested for V1.

INTENDED_EFFECT_FOR_PREPARATION: Windows 11 and Ubuntu Desktop remain the V1 supported and tested platforms for functional, restart/restore, special-window, privacy, container, group, backup/import and failure-boundary evidence (T01 functional scope unchanged).

Performance and resource evidence (r6 §9.1 targets, §9.3 T05-R2 L10/B300, the measurement-method binding including calibration and known uncertainty, and add-on memory/peak instruments) is required on Ubuntu Desktop only.
No resource or performance claim is made for Windows; where WindowSafe states its resource behavior, the Ubuntu-only verification is stated visibly.
F01 consequence once bound: the Windows add-on hard-peak instrument and the Windows calibration/interval/PID-coverage gates no longer apply; the Ubuntu calibration gate remains.
F05 consequence once bound: Windows native evidence remains functional; R500/R2000/H and L10/B300 measurements are Ubuntu-only.
